column3: The Hebrew explicitly repeats “morning”; BSB varies the second occurrence as “dawn.”
The Hebrew uses the image of making salvation and desire sprout; BSB renders it as bringing them about.
The Hebrew speaks of taking the thorns in the hand; BSB uses “gathered by hand.”
The Hebrew joins iron and the spear shaft with “and”; BSB uses “or.” It emphatically says that they will be burned, where BSB says that fire burns them to ashes.
The Hebrew includes the name Adino the Eznite; BSB instead says “He wielded his spear.”
The Hebrew says that the Philistines gathered “there”; BSB names Pas-dammim.
The Hebrew has an unnamed pronoun subject and says that his hand stuck to “the sword”; BSB names Eleazar and uses “his sword.” BSB also supplies “the dead” as the object of plundering.
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed; BSB supplies “Shammah.”
The Hebrew calls Benaiah the son of a valiant man; BSB calls Benaiah himself a man of valor.
The Hebrew repeatedly names “the Egyptian” but does not name Benaiah; BSB supplies Benaiah and replaces one occurrence of “the Egyptian” with a pronoun.
The Hebrew says he was honored above the Thirty; BSB says he was most honored among them.
The Hebrew places only Asahel explicitly “among the Thirty”; BSB supplies an introductory statement applying membership to the list.
The Hebrew names Heleb; BSB names Heled.
